question: Applying a tight tourniquet above a snakebite wound is recommended first aid because it prevents venom from entering the systemic circulation.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is FALSE. Tourniquets are contraindicated in snakebite first aid. Venom enters systemic circulation via lymphatics, not just blood vessels, so compression cannot stop envenomation. Correct first aid: immobilise the bitten limb, keep it at heart level, apply a pressure immobilisation bandage only for elapid (neurotoxic) bites, and transport immediately.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is FALSE. Tourniquets do NOT prevent systemic envenomation. Venom enters lymphatics and bloodstream rapidly and cannot be stopped by limb compression. Tourniquets cause ischaemia, necrosis, and compartment syndrome, and cause a dangerous surge of venom on release.
